Can a tested product photography prompt guarantee the same output if the model ID and seed are not recorded? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
No, a tested product photography prompt cannot guarantee the same output if the model ID and seed are not recorded.
In AI image generation, text prompts do not function like exact blueprints; instead, they act as general guides. Achieving pixel-perfect replication requires strict control over the stochastic (randomized) variables built into AI diffusion models. 
twinailabs.com
 +1
The primary reasons a prompt alone fails to guarantee identical results include:
1. The Critical Role of the Seed
Modern image AI models do not pull pre-made photos from a database; they start with a canvas of random digital noise (similar to television static) and mathematically sculpt it into an image based on your prompt. 
Runway
 +1
The Noise Pattern: The seed is the numerical value that initializes this starting noise pattern. 
Morphic
 +1
The Stochastic Path: If a seed is not specified, the system automatically uses a random number generator to pick a new one each time. A different seed will force the AI down a entirely unique mathematical path, altering the product's placement, light reflections, background framing, and overall composition—even if the prompt remains identical. 
Replicate
 +2
According to documentation from Runway and Morphic AI, locking the exact seed acts as the reproducibility anchor, allowing for identical or near-identical results. 
Non-Human Identity Management Group
 +2
2. Model Divergence and Updates
Even if you somehow guess the exact seed, your output will still differ wildly without the correct model ID. 
Pencil AI
Interpretation Variance: Different AI models interpret vocabulary, texture, lighting, and product fidelity in completely unique ways. For instance, a prompt run on Midjourney will produce drastically different aesthetics than the same prompt run on Stable Diffusion or Flux. 
Facebook
·Picsart
 +2
Underlying Infrastructure Changes: As noted in research hosted on Manuel Garcia's AI Guide, service providers constantly push minor updates, patches, or configuration changes to their platforms. If a platform alters its underlying model weights or deployment dependencies, an identical prompt will suddenly yield completely altered outputs. 
manuelgarcia.info
 +1
Comparison of Key Variables
Control Element	What It Directs	Can It Replicate Without Seed/Model ID?
Prompt	The subject, lighting style, and camera angle guidelines.	No. It only guarantees the theme, not the visual structure.
Model ID	The specific aesthetic intelligence, training data biases, and rendering style.	No. Different models interpret identical words differently.
Seed	The exact initial noise coordinates mapping out the composition.	No. A randomized seed completely re-shuffles the image layout.
Ultimately, for commercial applications like product photography where visual consistency across a brand catalog is vital, relying solely on text prompts is insufficient. To maintain a precise visual baseline, creators must archive the prompt, model version, seed, aspect ratio, and sampling steps.
